svg.title: Multi-Source BFS Frontier Rings and 0-1 BFS Double-Ended Queue
svg.desc: Animated visualization of Multi-Source BFS expanding simultaneously from two t=0 sources across a 5x4 grid in lockstep distance rings, paired with 0-1 BFS using a deque to push weight-0 edges to the front and weight-1 edges to the back in O(V+E) time.
svg.text: Multi-Source BFS & 0-1 BFS (Double-Ended Queue)
Lockstep Level-by-Level Frontier Expansion vs O(V+E) Shortest Path with Weights in {0, 1}
1. Multi-Source BFS (Proximity Grid, Sources at t=0)
Single O(V + E) pass
Sources S1(0,0) and S2(3,4) enter FIFO Queue simultaneously:
FIFO QUEUE & LEVEL WAVEFRONT TRACE:

g.text: Both sources start at distance 0 simultaneously. Avoids running S separate
t = 1: Pop S1 & S2 -> Enqueue 4 neighbors at d = 1
Every cell is marked visited AT ENQUEUE TIME (never twice!).
t = 2: Expand d = 1 ring -> Enqueue 6 cells at d = 2
Wavefronts from S1 and S2 advance in lockstep toward the middle.
Queue maintains strict non-decreasing distance order.
t = 3: Wavefronts collide! Remaining 8 cells receive d = 3
First source to reach each cell guarantees shortest unweighted distance.
All 20 cells resolved in a single O(V + E) pass!

svg.text: BFS Invariant:
The FIFO queue holds at most two consecutive distance levels: d and d+1.
For weighted {0, 1} edges, standard FIFO breaks -> upgrade to 0-1 BFS Deque!
2. 0-1 BFS (Deque: pushFront w=0, pushBack w=1)
O(V + E) vs Dijkstra O(E log V)
DEQUE STATE (Monotonic Order Preserved Without Heap!):
<- pushFront (w = 0)
pushBack (w = 1) ->

g.text: Pop S from front and relax outgoing edges (S,A) w=0 and (S,B) w=1.
A stays ahead of B because d(A)=0 < d(B)=1!
Deque remains sorted [0, 1, 1]: C:0 will be popped before B:1 and D:1!
DONE: dist = { S:0, A:0, C:0, B:1, D:1 }
Step 4: All shortest {0, 1} paths settled in O(V + E)!
Relax only when dist[u] + w < dist[v] (no visited[] freeze on w=1 first).

svg.text: Why 0-1 BFS Beats Dijkstra Without a Binary Heap
At any instant, the deque contains nodes at only TWO distances: d and d+1.
Weight-0 pushes to front (d + 0 = d); weight-1 pushes to back (d + 1).
O(1) deque ops -> drops O((V+E) log V) down to strictly O(V+E)!
BFS Family Invariants:
Source (d=0) / w=0 pushFront
d=1 wave / w=1 pushBack
d=2 wave
d=3 collision wave
Gotcha in 0-1 BFS: check `if (dist[u] + w < dist[v])` before pushing, and skip stale entries (`if (d > dist[u]) continue`) because a node can be pushed at d+1 then relaxed to d via a 0-edge.
